transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Lumera - Head of ML), Samir Patel (Lumera CTO), Nora Kim (Data Eng), Jamal Ortiz (Clinical SME)

Summary (auto):
Discussed POC success criteria for clinical extraction and ICD mapping, workload sizing (expected QPS, tokens per request), open-model shortlist for multilingual extraction (EN/ES/FR), bench plan including latency and quality metrics, and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Action items captured.

[00:00] Avery (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we got about an hour, real quick intros?
[00:06] Elena: Hi, Elena Ruiz, Head of ML at Lumera, we run clinical NLP for lab reports and discharge summaries.
[00:10] Samir: Samir Patel, CTO. We're focused on integrating models into our triage and coding pipelines.
[00:14] Nora: Nora, data eng, I handle ingestion and de-id.
[00:17] Jamal: Jamal, clinical SME, I'll validate clinical labels.
[00:20] Avery: Great, Mateo and I from Redwood — Mateo will cover benchmarks and infra details.

[00:35] Mateo (SE): Cool thanks. High level agenda: confirm success criteria, size the workload (throughput/latency/cost targets), pick 3-4 open model candidates for the POC, and agree bench plan + timeline.
[00:44] Elena: Sounds good. Our immediate problem: extract structured lab values, units, normalization, and map diagnoses to ICD-10. Must support English and Spanish primarily, French second. Accuracy is top priority — false positives on abnormal labs are costly.

[01:10] Jamal: To add, we need entity-level precision for critical fields: test name, numeric value, unit, normal-range flag. For ICD mapping we want high recall but precision matters for billing.

[01:30] Avery: Understood. Quick qualification: are you ok with a hosted POC to start, or do you require private VPC / on-prem from day one?
[01:39] Samir: For the POC we can start on hosted but data must be de-identified. If results look good we'll move to Private (VPC) before production. Also we'll need SOC 2 and encryption at rest — KMS integration.
[01:50] Avery: Yep we can start hosted; we'll share SOC 2 and SSO docs. Mateo can speak to KMS options for Private later.

[02:10] Mateo: On workload sizing — what's your expected concurrency and request profile?
[02:15] Nora: We'll batch documents from an ingest queue. Peak concurrent workers ~12, average qps ~35–45 during processing windows. Typical document size is 800–1,500 tokens after tokenization, but the extraction prompt plus system context averages to ~120-250 tokens per request returned.
[02:37] Mateo: Great, so plan bench targets around 40 QPS with p50 latency < 250ms and p95 < 800ms for the extraction-only path. Does that align with expectations?
[02:48] Samir: Yes, p50 < 250ms is ideal. We can accept higher p95 during POC if necessary while optimizing batching/kv cache.

[03:05] Elena: Cost target is also important — we'd like to keep inference cost similar to $0.0015–0.003 per input token ideally for scale, but we'll prioritize quality over cost for this initial POC.

[03:20] Mateo: Noted. For the model shortlist we typically pick a gradient: smaller faster model, medium-quality with good instruction tuning, and one larger model for upper-bound quality. Proposed candidates (open models):
- Llama-3-13B (q4_0) — expected good EN quality, decent multilingual with instruction tuning
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4) — very efficient, good for constrained latency/cost
- Falcon-40B-instruct (quant) — higher quality for extraction, heavier but useful for upper-bound
- Mixtral / xP3 variant (we mentioned mixtral) — optional, depending on license

[04:10] Elena: Curious about Spanish/French capability — historically the 13B Llama lineage handled Spanish okay, but we have domain-specific terms and abbreviations. Falcon-40B might do better but cost/latency worry.
[04:23] Mateo: Right. We will include an explicit multilingual bench with spanish-fr test set; we'll evaluate on both token-level extraction F1 and a normalized-value accuracy metric.

[04:40] Jamal: What metrics are you proposing? For lab values I'd like exact numeric match after normalization (within 1% or unit corrected). For entities, span-level F1; for ICD mapping, top-1 accuracy and top-3 recall.

[04:54] Mateo: Proposed metrics:
- Entity extraction: span-level micro-F1 (primary)
- Numeric normalization: exact-match percentage after unit conversion
- ICD mapping: top-1 accuracy and top-3 recall
- Latency: p50/p95
- Cost: tokens/second and per-request cost estimate

[05:15] Samir: Sounds good. Also want a degradation plan — if the top model drops in availability we need fallback to a smaller model with quality delta bounded.

[05:27] Avery: Redwood supports routing by policy and can automatically fallback to a compatible variant. We can capture quality deltas in bench so you can set a threshold for auto-fallback.

[05:40] Mateo: For bench plan timeline: Week 0 (this week) — finalize success criteria & sample set; Week 1 — run single-instance quality evals across the 3 models; Week 2 — run throughput/latency tests (Dedicated pool sim) and begin tuning batching/cache; Week 3 — integrate with a small end-to-end run and compare costs; Week 4 — wrap-up and recommendation. Does a 4-week POC fit your procurement/calendar?
[06:03] Elena: Yes 4 weeks is fine. Procurement has to sign a simple MSA though. Samir, can procurement turn around in 2 weeks?
[06:10] Samir: Likely — we need price numbers for Dedicated as well to include in approvals.

[06:20] Nora: On data — we'll provide 500 de-id examples spanning EN/ES/FR across lab reports and discharge notes. Is that enough for a first pass?
[06:27] Mateo: 500 is a good starting set especially if it's balanced across languages and entities. For better signal on ICD mapping we'll need ~200 labeled mapping examples.

[06:37] Jamal: We'll prioritize the critical lab tests and 5 common ICD clusters for the POC.

[06:45] Elena: One other point — we have an internal mapping pipeline that prefers deterministic rules for certain lab conversions. We want the model to output in a structured JSON that our parser can consume, with fields: test_name, value, unit, normalized_value, unit_standard, icd_candidates (list).

[07:00] Mateo: We'll include structured output prompts and evaluate parseability and schema conformance as part of the bench. Redwood supports structured output enforcement and schema hints at the API level.

[07:12] Avery: Regarding security & compliance, we'll push the SOC 2 artifact and SSO integration guide. Samir, you mentioned a VPC step later — for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
[07:24] Samir: Good. Also need to confirm data retention/SLA for logs during the POC.

[07:32] Mateo: We can configure shorter retention for POC logs; we'll add that to the security call.

[07:40] Elena: Bench specifics — how will you measure numeric normalization robustness? Some reports list ranges like "<5" or "<0.1" which are tricky for strict equality.

[07:50] Jamal: Right, we need fuzzy-matching rules — we'll annotate the expected normalized value and a normalization confidence.

[08:00] Mateo: We'll add a tolerance rule to the numeric metric: exact-match or within a 5% tolerance or flagged as a range; we'll report normalized-confidence separately.

[08:12] Elena: On the shortlist — could you add an MPT-style model to the bench? We heard a fork has decent multilingual behavior.
[08:18] Mateo: Sure, we can add MPT-30B-instruct (quant) as an optional run if license fits. That gives us another mid-high quality point. We'll keep it optional to control run time/cost.

[08:32] Samir: What's the estimated cost/time to run the full bench on Redwood Dedicated? Ballpark for 40 QPS emulation for an hour?
[08:40] Mateo: Ballpark: small models (7–13B) are cheap; the 40B class for throughput runs shifts to larger GPUs or multi-GPU config. Rough estimate: a single 1-hour throughput run across 3 models might be $600–1,800 depending on model sizes and quantization. We'll give precise numbers in the cost sheet.

[09:00] Elena: Okay. Also want an eval for hallucination risk — for ICD mapping false positives are dangerous. Can you include a hallucination false-positive rate?

[09:08] Mateo: Yes, we'll include a "hallucination/unsupported entity" metric: rate at which model invents a test or maps to an ICD when none exist. We'll prioritize low hallucination.

[09:20] Avery: Quick note: you mentioned bilingual UI — do you need real-time API streaming for low-latency interactive use or is batch processing enough?
[09:28] Elena: Batch first. We may need streaming in phase 2 for clinician-facing features.

[09:34] Mateo: Great; bench will focus on batch and high-throughput inference.

[09:42] Jamal: For validation we'll do human review on a 10% sample and generate error taxonomy (unit mismatch, wrong test name, mapping errors).

[09:52] Nora: About dataset delivery, we will upload to a secured S3 with pre-signed URLs; can Redwood pick that up?
[09:58] Avery: Yes, we can pull from S3 or you can upload to a Redwood staging bucket for the POC — we'll send the upload instructions.

[10:08] Mateo: One technical detail: we'll evaluate two prompt strategies — direct extraction prompts vs. schema-first (few-shot structured examples). We'll log token counts for both to assess cost tradeoffs.

[10:22] Elena: Kudos. For the schema-first approach, we might insert a short clinical ontology mapping snippet — hope it won't explode token counts.

[10:29] Mateo: We'll measure prompt size impact. For larger ontologies we can use context caching or external KV to avoid repeating the whole ontology each request. We'll test prefix/KV cache effectiveness during Week 2.

[10:42] Samir: Regarding SLA in production, if we go Dedicated, what's Redwood's typical SLA for uptime and latency?
[10:48] Avery: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and a latency target by model class; we can include proposed numbers in the Dedicated quote.

[10:55] Elena: Can Redwood provide an initial mapping of which model is likely to meet our p50/p95 targets? A quick heuristic is useful for procurement.

[11:05] Mateo: Heuristic: Mistral-7B / MPT-30B on well-tuned quant runs will likely meet p50 200–300ms for the requested document size when using batching. Llama-3-13B a bit higher but close. Falcon-40B quant will give the best extraction quality but p50 will be higher and costs more. We'll provide a short one-pager with expected latency/cost per model.

[11:25] Jamal: What about tokenization differences across models — will that affect numeric extraction?

[11:30] Mateo: Tokenization affects token counts/cost but for numeric extraction we use normalized outputs (strings/numbers) so tokenization variance is secondary to model reasoning about numeric entities. Still we'll normalize after the model output, and include tokenization overhead in cost calc.

[11:45] Avery: Let's recap next steps and owners — Elena to confirm final success thresholds and upload samples; Nora to deliver the 500 de-id records; Avery to share bench spreadsheet and model shortlist; Mateo to produce Dedicated cost estimate and bench plan. Security team to get SOC 2 artifacts to Samir.

[12:05] Elena: We'll aim to have thresholds confirmed by Friday (2026-10-15).
[12:10] Samir: Procurement and legal will need the MSA; I'll have procurement reach out.

[12:18] Nora: I'll start packaging the data and will flag any PII concerns.

[12:25] Avery: Great, we'll schedule the bench kickoff for Monday 2026-10-20. Mateo, can you own the bench run coordination that week?

[12:30] Mateo: Yup I'll coordinate.

[12:35] Jamal: One last quick question — for ICD mapping, are you planning to allow model to suggest multiple candidates with confidences?

[12:40] Mateo: Yes, we'll capture top-3 candidates with confidence scores in the schema. We'll measure top-1 accuracy and top-3 recall.

[12:50] Avery: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and the spreadsheet after the call. Any final questions?
[12:55] Elena: No, thanks.
[12:58] Samir: Thanks all.
[13:00] Meeting end.

References/links mentioned: bench spreadsheet (link to be sent), SOC2 artifact (to be shared), S3 upload instructions (to be shared).

Artifacts attached later: bench plan (week-by-week), model shortlist and cost estimate, sample mapping schema.
